question.text: As described on page 121 of the NISM Series-XVI (December 2025) workbook, an Associated Person engaging with clients on behalf of a commodity Trading Member must:

answer.text: Route all monetary transactions of clients directly through the Trading Member/broker and not handle client funds directly themselves
Maintain their own clearing account with the clearing corporation
Be a separately SEBI-registered intermediary independent of the Trading Member

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (NISM Series-XVI December 2025, p.121) attaches the routed-monetary-transactions and certification language to an Associated Person engaging with clients on behalf of a Trading Member. All client money therefore moves through the broker, never the Associated Person directly. The Associated Person is an extension of the broker, not an independent intermediary. The Trap: Associated Persons do not hold their own clearing accounts, exchange memberships, or separate SEBI registrations - they operate under the broker's framework. The audit flagged the original because the stem used "Authorized Person (AP)", but page 121 attaches the routed-money/certification rules to "Associated Person"; AP migration (existing sub-brokers becoming Authorized Persons or Trading Members) is a separate topic on the same page. The abbreviation AP was therefore ambiguous between the two roles. Note: The original was ambiguous because "AP" could mean either "Authorized Person" or "Associated Person", and only the Associated Person framing matches the routed-monetary-transactions answer. The stem has been changed to "Associated Person" (referencing p.121 of NISM Series-XVI December 2025), which uniquely supports the keyed option.
